## What We Did
Covered LISA, and what makes it different than Moran's I (local v. global)

## Key Concepts
LISA: Local Indicators of Spatial Association
- Local Moran's I, one house at a time
- spatial clusters of errors

Types of LISA observations, in our Chicago house price example:
high-high: underpredicted pocket; a missing amenity
high-low: underpredicted house; something about the house itself
low-high: overpredicted house; something about the house
low-low: overpredicted pocket; a missing disamenity
"is my house priced similarly to houses adjacent to it, or is there something about my house in particular?"

nb2listw(): creates a neighbor weight matrix
near features options:
- radial buffer
- nearest feature
- k-nearest neighbor

## Reflection
Overall, I found the conversation on LISA to be interesting. We had already covered this in statistics, so it wasn't covering new ground either. But, it wasn't very thoroughly there, so it was good to see yet another example of it in application.
